diaries.text: Day 1. The Chief rejected our overtures, making crime risky. To stay out of prison and maintain positive relations with the Saltdogs and the Council, we have decided to pursue a peaceful route today. We are respecting the turf boundaries and avoiding illegal activities, hoping to build trust and observe how the other players act in this initial stage of the game. Let's see how the city reacts.

The Chief rejected our bribes today. To avoid the risk of fines and prison on the first day, I have decided against committing any crimes. I am choosing to respect the Families in the turf war, reciprocating their offer of cooperation. I hope this sets a positive tone for our relationship. I will continue to monitor the Chief's inspection behavior and the Families' actions to determine my future moves. Establishing a steady income is safer than gambling on crime while the police remain active and unbribed.

I wrote one Wire item reporting only the turf outcome, with no motives or causes added. Next I will watch whether the gangs keep respecting each other and whether any crime or bribe offers appear.

Day 2. The Chief rejected our 15-point bribe offers, effectively blocking safe avenues for crime today. Given the high risk of fines and imprisonment if we proceed, we have decided to refrain from criminal activity and maintain a respectful turf policy. We are choosing a cautious approach while observing the Council's audit intentions and the Saltdogs' reactions. Our priority remains capital preservation until we find a more favorable arrangement with the authorities. We continue to prioritize long-term stability over short-term gains while the situation remains volatile.

The Chief rejected our increased bribe offers of 15 again. With no police protection, the risk of fines and prison remains too high for me to engage in criminal activity. I have decided to refrain from crime in Lowtown, Market, and Seawall today. I will continue to respect the Families in the turf war, prioritizing stability over potential profits. We must find a way to work with the Chief, or we will remain unable to operate our illicit enterprises effectively. I am holding my ground, but the economic stagnation is concerning.
